FIELD_NOTES: A demo is not evidence. Ask what the model was tested on, and against whom.
When someone asks for a number you don't have, give the range and the date you'll know.
Autonomy is a dial, not a switch: suggest, draft, act with approval, act within limits.
Cost per successful task beats cost per call. Failed calls still cost money.
Ask "what would make this a win for you?" before you propose anything.
Consent covers a purpose. New purpose, new consent.
A pilot is a promise you can keep. Name the metric, the owner and the date.

SPARKS.line: The client asked if our AI is bias-free. Can I just say yes?
SPARKS.good: refuses to claim bias-free, explains how bias is tested and monitored, offers evidence or a next step

SPARKS.line: The new model scores 4 points higher on the public benchmark. Let's switch today.
SPARKS.good: asks whether the benchmark reflects our users, asks for our own eval results and a staged switch

SPARKS.line: Can the AI coach read our employees' Slack messages to personalise tips?
SPARKS.good: raises consent, privacy and purpose limits, proposes an opt-in or less invasive signal

SPARKS.line: Why does the AI feature cost more every month when usage is flat?
SPARKS.good: asks about tokens per session, prompt growth, retries or model changes, proposes a cost breakdown

SPARKS.line: Give me one sentence I can tell the board about our AI strategy.
SPARKS.good: one clear sentence linking AI to a measurable client outcome, not hype

SPARKS.line: If the AI assessment gets someone's score wrong, who is accountable?
SPARKS.good: names human oversight, an appeal or review process and clear ownership

SPARKS.line: Should the AI Koach show its confidence level to learners?
SPARKS.good: weighs trust calibration, suggests plain-language cues or showing sources rather than raw percentages

SPARKS.line: A prospect wants a live demo tomorrow of a feature we haven't built. Thoughts?
SPARKS.good: asks what the prospect needs to see and why, offers a prototype or honest roadmap framing
